title: AI Agents com ADK
tagline: Intelligent agents integrated into the GCP ecosystem via MCP Toolbox
summary: Autonomous agents integrating Jira, Looker, and BigQuery via MCP Toolbox, deployed on Cloud Run with Vertex AI.
context: The team needed intelligent agents that could query business data in Jira, Looker, and BigQuery autonomously, without exposing internal APIs directly to the model.
challenges: Orchestrate multiple tools (Jira, Looker, BigQuery) reliably without the agent entering loops
Ensure security access to sensitive data via MCP Toolbox in the GCP environment
Manage context and memory in long conversations without exceeding token limits
Deploy on Cloud Run with acceptable cold start for interactive use
learnings: Describe tools with concrete examples of when not using them reduces unnecessary calls by ~40%
Separate agents by domain is more robust than a generic agent with many tools
Structured logs of each agent decision are essential for production debugging

title: Payment Integration Platform
tagline: Stripe event-driven: checkout, subscriptions, and lifecycle management
summary: Complete integration with Stripe — webhooks, automatic checkout, subscription management, and automatic payment failure recovery.
context: The product needed to support recurring payments with multiple plans, upgrades, and downgrades in real time, and automatic recovery of payment failures.
challenges: Ensure idempotency in Stripe webhook processing
Synchronize subscription state between Stripe and the local database
Manage plan transitions with correct prorated values
Recover payment failures with intelligent retry
learnings: Test webhooks locally with Stripe CLI before production saves hours of debugging
Log the complete event payload facilitates payment dispute auditing
Implement webhook delivery log allows reprocessing events manually

title: GPOS Payment System
tagline: Backend .NET/C# for PIX and cards with mTLS authentication
summary: Complete payment system in .NET/C# with PIX, cards, mTLS, and remote terminal registration — eliminating the physical device shipping process.
context: The GPOS product needed a robust backend to process payments via PIX and cards, with mutual authentication between physical terminals and the server, and remote registration of new devices.
challenges: Implement mTLS for mutual authentication between physical terminals and the server
Ensure compliance with BACEN rules for PIX transactions
Eliminate the manual physical device shipping process for registration
Maintain transactional consistency in unstable connection scenarios
learnings: BACEN documentation for PIX is extensive but precise — following it exactly avoids rejections
Implement circuit breaker in PSP calls to prevent cascading failures
Immutable transaction logs are mandatory for auditing

title: Transactional Email Microservice
tagline: Decoupled microservice with message queue for email sending
summary: Decoupled microservice with message queue, reused across multiple products without code changes.
context: Multiple products of the company needed to send transactional emails — confirmation, notification, alerts. Each product had its own duplicated implementation.
challenges: Decouple the email sending completely from the business logic of the products
Ensure reliable delivery even when the SMTP provider is unavailable
Support dynamic templates without requiring a deploy for each content change
learnings: Dead letter queue is essential — without it, failed emails are lost silently
Rate limiting on the consumer avoids banning the SMTP provider by sending in bursts

title: Computer Vision Analytics
tagline: People counting and stay time for operational metrics
summary: Computer vision pipeline for people counting and stay time analysis generating operational metrics in real time.
context: Operations needed to understand flow in physical spaces to optimize resources and scale of service.
challenges: Detect and track people with acceptable precision on limited hardware
Calculate stay time even with partial camera occlusion
Aggregate metrics in real time without overloading the database
learnings: Calibrate the entry/exit counting line requires physical tests in the physical space
Lighting varies a lot throughout the day — histogram normalization improves consistency

title: Service Licensing System
tagline: Token activation, permission management, and administrative CRUDs
summary: Service licensing system with token activation, granular permission control, and complete administrative panel.
context: The product needed to control access to features by license plan, with self-service activation and centralized administrative management.
challenges: Model granular permissions by feature without exploding the schema complexity
Token activation flow with expiration and unique invalidation
Complete administrative panel with CRUDs
learnings: Never store tokens in plain text — even activation tokens must be hashed
Audit log in a separate table for each permission mutation is essential
